Paramagnetism depends on unpaired electrons: For tetrahedral d-electron configurations, high-spin is typical; Co2+ (d7) in tetrahedral has 3 unpaired electrons → paramagnetic; Ni2+ (d8) in tetrahedral has 2 unpaired electrons → paramagnetic. Square planar d8 (Pt2+) is diamagnetic; octahedral low-spin d6 (Fe2+ in CN-) is diamagnetic; octahedral high-spin d3 (Cr3+) and d4 (V3+) are paramagnetic but geometry is octahedral, not sp3. Thus only tetrahedral complexes with paramagnetism and sp3 hybridisation are considered. Among the list, [CoCl4]2- and [NiCl4]2- are tetrahedral and paramagnetic. [PtCl4]2- is square planar (dsp2) and diamagnetic; [Cr(H2O)6]3+, [V(H2O)6]3+, [Fe(H2O)6]3+ are octahedral; [Fe(CN)6]4- is octahedral low-spin diamagnetic; [Ni(CO)4] is tetrahedral but Ni0 d10 diamagnetic. Hence total number of species that are paramagnetic and have sp3 hybridisation = 2.
